title: Naomi and Ruth Return to Bethlehem
summary: In the days of the judges a famine drives Elimelech and Naomi of Bethlehem and their sons to Moab. Elimelech dies, the sons marry Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth, and then both sons die. Naomi decides to return when she hears the LORD has given Judah food, and urges her daughters-in-law to go home. Orpah turns back, but Ruth clings to Naomi and says, 'thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.' They reach Bethlehem at the barley harvest.

title: Ruth Gleans in Boaz's Field
summary: Ruth goes to glean in the fields and happens on the land of Boaz, a wealthy relative of Elimelech. Boaz has heard of her loyalty to Naomi, tells her to stay with his young women and drink from the men's water, and instructs his workers to leave extra grain. At mealtime he shares bread and roasted grain with her. She brings home about an ephah of barley, and Naomi blesses Boaz and says he is one of their near kinsmen.

title: The Threshing Floor
summary: Naomi tells Ruth to wash, anoint herself and put on her best clothes and go to the threshing floor at night, where Boaz will be sleeping. After he lies down, Ruth uncovers his feet and lies at them. Startled at midnight, Boaz hears her ask him to spread his skirt over her as a near kinsman. He blesses her, says there is a closer relative, promises to act as redeemer if that man will not, and sends her home before morning with six measures of barley.

title: Boaz Redeems and Marries Ruth
summary: At the city gate Boaz asks the nearer kinsman, before ten elders, whether he will redeem Elimelech's land. The man agrees until he learns that he must also take Ruth, and then gives up his right, confirming it by handing over his sandal. Boaz buys the land and takes Ruth as his wife, and the women bless Naomi when Ruth bears Obed, who becomes the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David. The book ends with a genealogy from Pharez to David.
